title: Storm-Damage Extension to the Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing Hardship Offer
content:
**Disaster relief bulletin — Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing.**

For a hardship request on an account whose plan carries no promotion (a fixed-rate or low-payment plan), the per-request cap of the hardship offer adds a storm-damage extension to the plan's maximum months per deferral, read from the customer's warranty claims discovered in the three months before the request: a glass-breakage claim and a frame-and-sash claim both on file add the double damage extension of 2 months; a glass-breakage claim or a frame-and-sash claim, but not both, adds the damage extension of 1 month; neither adds nothing.

## Which claims count

The claims are the customer's warranty claims under Warranty Coverage whose covered component is glass breakage or frame and sash, and whose discovery date — the date the customer states the problem was first noticed — falls in the three months before the hardship request. Claims for any other component (an insulated glass seal, hardware, a screen, weatherstrip, exterior finish or installation workmanship) do not count.

## Extension table

| Glass-breakage claim discovered in the three months | Frame-and-sash claim discovered in the three months | Added to the plan's maximum months per deferral |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 2 months |
| Yes | No | 1 month |
| No | Yes | 1 month |
| No | No | Nothing |

Several claims for the same component count as that component being on file once: two glass-breakage claims and no frame-and-sash claim add 1 month.

## Hypothetical cases

- A glass-breakage claim discovered one month before the request and a frame-and-sash claim discovered two months before it: 2 months added.
- A frame-and-sash claim discovered five months before the request and nothing since: outside the three months, nothing added.
- A hardware claim discovered last week: not a counted component, nothing added.
